title: ViewSets and Routers
description: Organize API endpoints using ViewSets and automatically generate URLs with routers.

slides.title: ViewSets: All Actions in One Class 🧩
slides.content:
A **ViewSet** is a class that groups all CRUD actions (list, create, retrieve, update, delete) for a resource. Instead of writing multiple views, you write one ViewSet and a **router** automatically generates the URL patterns.

DRF provides `ModelViewSet` which includes default implementations for standard actions.

slides.title: Creating a ViewSet
slides.content:
from rest_framework import viewsets
from .models import Post
from .serializers import PostSerializer

class PostViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    queryset = Post.objects.all()
    serializer_class = PostSerializer

quizData.question: Which ViewSet includes built‑in actions for list, create, retrieve, update, and delete?
quizData.explanation: `ModelViewSet` provides full CRUD actions. `ViewSet` is a base class, `GenericViewSet` provides base methods for custom actions.

slides.title: Using Routers
slides.content:
# urls.py
from django.urls import path, include
from rest_framework.routers import DefaultRouter
from .views import PostViewSet

router = DefaultRouter()
router.register(r'posts', PostViewSet)  # registers /posts/ endpoint

urlpatterns = [
    path('', include(router.urls)),
]

# This automatically creates:
# GET    /posts/          → list
# POST   /posts/          → create
# GET    /posts/{id}/     → retrieve
# PUT    /posts/{id}/     → update
# DELETE /posts/{id}/     → destroy

slides.title: Custom Actions
Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `router` to keep your URLs DRY

Routers automatically generate URLs, reducing boilerplate. You can also mix router URLs with custom URL patterns.
